Set up the module object for GeM (MY)

Source: R/adult-MY-GeM.R
setup_MY_obj.GeM.Rd

Set up a GeM module object for the MY component and the \(s^{th}\) vector species.

  • Set the module name to GeM.

  • Create the module object with make_MY_obj_GeM, passing nPatches and options.

  • Set the skill set using get_skillset_MY.

  • Initialize the circadian function using setup_F_circadian.setup.

  • Initialize the mosquito demographic matrix port.

  • Initialize the EIP survival and dispersal matrix port.

  • Initialize the mosquito dispersal matrix using setup_K_matrix.zero.

  • Set initial values using setup_MY_inits, passing options to override defaults.

  • Return the updated xds model object.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'GeM'
setup_MY_obj(MYname, xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1)

Arguments

MYname

the name of the model

xds_obj

an xds model object

options

a list

s

the vector species index

Value

an xds model object

Note

The module object is stored at xds_obj$MY_obj[[s]] Its class is set to GeM.

State Variables

M

density of adult mosquitoes

P

density of parous adult mosquitoes

Y

density of infected adult mosquitoes

Z

density of infectious adult mosquitoes

Parameters

f

blood feeding rate — use setup_f or setup_blood_feeding_rates

q

human fraction — use setup_q or setup_human_fractions

g

mosquito mortality rate — use setup_g or setup_mosquito_mortality

eip or \(\tau\)

extrinsic incubation period — use setup_eip

sigma or \(\sigma\)

emigration rate — use setup_sigma or setup_mosy_emigration

mu or \(\mu\)

emigration loss fraction — use setup_mu or setup_emigration_loss

K or K_matrix

mosquito dispersal matrix — use setup_K_matrix

nu or \(\nu\)

oviposition rate: the number of egg batches laid in each patch, per mosquito, per day — use setup_nu or setup_egg_batch_rates

eggs_per_batch

number of eggs per batch

After basic setup, change_MY_pars.GeM can be used to change static parameter values. By default, bionomic parameters are configured as static baselines; advanced setup can be used to define dynamic ports.

EIP

Let \(\tau(t)\) be the EIP for a mosquito infected at time \(t\); it becomes infectious at time \(t+\tau(t)\). Let \(\tau'(t)\) be the elapsed time since infection for a mosquito that becomes infectious at time \(t\). These quantities satisfy $$\tau(t)=\tau'(t+\tau(t)) \qquad \tau'(t)=\tau(t-\tau'(t)).$$ The F_eip function returns the lag \(\tau'(t)\) used by the delay equations. A time-varying EIP also requires its derivative, computed by dF_eip.

Accessory Variable

The matrix \(\Upsilon(t)\) represents survival and dispersal through the time-varying EIP, from \(t_\tau=t-\tau'(t)\) to \(t\). In the autonomous case it is \(e^{-\Omega\tau}\). For time-varying demography and EIP, it is computed as an accessory variable: $$\frac{d\Upsilon}{dt}=\left(\Omega(t_\tau)\left(1-\frac{d\tau'(t)}{dt}\right)-\Omega(t)\right)\cdot\Upsilon(t).$$ The initial matrix is set to \(\exp(-\Omega eip)\). This variable is internal to the model and is not an output orbit.
